title: A frontier generator for library upgrades

blocks.text: A county library system has a budget for branch upgrades. Each upgrade adds opening hours per week and reading-room seats, both whole numbers, and has a cost. The board wants to see every choice worth considering: the full list of (hours, seats) scores that no other affordable choice beats on both or ties on one and beats on the other.

Write `frontier(upgrades, budget)` in `libraries.py`. It returns every Pareto-optimal score as a list of `(hours, seats)` pairs, sorted by hours (fewest first), each listed once. The starter builds the model, its budget row and the two objective expressions; you write the generator. Use any method from the lesson; whichever you pick, make sure a tie on one objective cannot leave a dominated score in the list.

If you pick AUGMECON (a seats floor with a slack, and a reward $`(\rho / r_2) \cdot s`$ on the slack, as in lesson 8.3.2), you need $`r_2`$. A lexicographic payoff table gives the exact range of seats, which bounds every slack when the first floor is the seats of the most-hours end, as in lesson 8.3.2. Any number at least as large as every slack your sweep can produce works as well, for example the total seats of all upgrades, which also covers a sweep that starts its floor at 0. With such an $`r_2`$, $`s / r_2 \le 1`$, so the reward is at most $`\rho`$ ($`10^{-3}`$ in the lesson), less than one hour; hours are whole numbers, so the reward can never pay for an hour and only chooses among choices tied on hours. Too small an $`r_2`$ breaks that: the reward can then outweigh an hour and trade hours for seats. The reference needs no $`r_2`$: at each floor it maximizes hours, then holds the hours and maximizes seats, two solves per floor.

Write down first what you solve at each floor (objective, floor row, any tie-breaking), and why it cannot miss a score. The tests list every affordable choice by hand and check your list against it, including that no score in it dominates another. About fifteen lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Upgrade:
    name: str
    hours: int        # opening hours added per week
    seats: int        # reading-room seats added
    cost: int         # $k


def solved(model: mathopt.Model) -> mathopt.SolveResult | None:
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=mathopt.SolveParameters(relative_gap_tolerance=0.0))
    return result if result.termination.reason == mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL else None


def frontier(upgrades: list[Upgrade], budget: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Every Pareto-optimal (hours, seats) score of the affordable choices, sorted by hours."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="libraries")
    pick = [model.add_binary_variable(name=f"do_{u.name}") for u in upgrades]
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(u.cost * v for u, v in zip(upgrades, pick)) <= budget, name="budget")
    hours = mathopt.LinearExpression() + sum(u.hours * v for u, v in zip(upgrades, pick))
    seats = mathopt.LinearExpression() + sum(u.seats * v for u, v in zip(upgrades, pick))
    points, need = [], 0
    while True:
        enough = model.add_linear_constraint(seats >= need, name="seat_floor")
        model.maximize(hours)
        first = solved(model)
        if first is None:
            break
        keep = model.add_linear_constraint(hours >= first.objective_value() - 1e-6, name="keep_hours")
        model.maximize(seats)
        second = solved(model).variable_values()
        h, s = round(mathopt.evaluate_expression(hours, second)), round(mathopt.evaluate_expression(seats, second))
        points.append((h, s))
        model.delete_linear_constraint(enough)
        model.delete_linear_constraint(keep)
        need = s + 1
    return sorted(points)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    plans = [Upgrade("Eastside", 12, 20, 40), Upgrade("Harbor", 20, 5, 35), Upgrade("Old Town", 6, 30, 30)]
    print(frontier(plans, 70))

with choices that tie on hours, no score returned is dominated by another
the most hours with no seats added at all is on the frontier
the scores are sorted by hours, fewest first

origin.section: Generate the Frontier Once, and Check That No Point Dominates Another

concepts: a generator that steps a whole-number floor and breaks ties returns every Pareto score once
a frontier is checked by comparing every pair before anyone reads it
